proofs.proof_tex:
Fix
\[
H=0,
\qquad p=S=d=1,
\qquad \lambda=\kappa=1,
\qquad \pi_1=1.
\tag{1}
\]
Choose
\[
B=16,
\quad c_X=C_X=c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1,
\quad \delta_0=\frac14,
\quad c_{\mathrm{mod}}=C_{\mathrm{mod}}=1,
\tag{2}
\]
take arbitrary fixed \(\beta_0>0\) and \(\rho_0\in(0,1)\), choose \(L\) at least the \(\mathcal H_1(1,\cdot)\)-radius of the affine function below, and let
\[
K(u)=\mathbf 1\{|u|\le1\}.
\tag{3}
\]
This kernel is nonnegative, bounded, compactly supported, and equal to one near zero.  Choose \(0<c_G\le1\).  By the definitions of \(r\), \(b_r\), and \(e_0\),
\[
r=\lceil1\rceil-1=0,
\qquad b_0(u)=e_0=1.
\tag{4}
\]
Let \(E_0\) be constant, set \(z_0=1/2\) and \(\mathcal Z_+=\{1/2\}\), and put \(n_1=N=T^2\).

We construct a family indexed by a number \(\eta\in(0,1)\).  Write \(X_t=X_{1t}\), and let \(X_1,\ldots,X_T\) be independent uniform variables on \([0,1]\).  Set
\[
m(x)=8+x-\frac12,
\qquad
Q_{1ti}=m(X_t)+\frac12U_{ti},
\tag{5}
\]
where the \(U_{ti}\) are mutually independent Rademacher variables, independent of the complete design.  Since \(m([0,1])=[15/2,17/2]\),
\[
7\le Q_{1ti}\le9\le B,
\qquad
\mathbb E[Q_{1ti}\mid X_t=x,E_0]=m(x).
\tag{6}
\]
Thus (6) verifies \(\texttt{ass:bounded-historical-wealth}\) and \(\texttt{ass:historical-regression}\).  The choice of \(L\) and the affine form in (5) verify \(\texttt{ass:holder-smoothness}\).  The density of each \(X_t\) equals one on \([0,1]\), verifying \(\texttt{ass:design-density}\).  Calendar independence gives, for every \(\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}\ge1\),
\[
\beta_P(\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}\mid E_0)=0
\le \beta_0\rho_0^{\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}},
\tag{7}
\]
which is \(\texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}\).  Finally, set \(X_{1t}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_t\), as required by \(\texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates}\).

Independently of the historical sample, let
\[
Z_j=\frac12+V_j,
\tag{8}
\]
where \(V_1,\ldots,V_N\) are independent Rademacher variables.  Equations (2) and (8) give
\[
\mathbb E[Z_j\mid E_0]=z_0,
\qquad
\Sigma=\operatorname{Var}(Z_j\mid E_0)=1,
\tag{9}
\]
and
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[
\left|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\right|^4\,\middle|\,E_0
\right]=1\le B.
\tag{10}
\]
Thus (8)--(10) verify \(\texttt{ass:donor-replication}\), \(\texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}\), and \(\texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment}\); the stipulated independence verifies \(\texttt{ass:donor-independence}\).  Since \(D=Sd=1\), (2) also has the strictly compatible envelope \(B>D^2\).

For \(0<\delta\le\delta_0\), every \(z_0+u\) with \(|u|\le\delta\) belongs to \([0,1]\).  From \(\Sigma=1\), \(\pi_1=1\), \(\texttt{def:local-modulus}\), and (5),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\omega_P(\delta;z_0)
&=\sup_{|u|\le\delta}|m(z_0+u)-m(z_0)|\\
&=\sup_{|u|\le\delta}|u|
=\delta.
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
Equation (11) verifies both halves of \(\texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus}\).  Moreover,
\[
\operatorname{dist}(z_0,\partial[0,1])=\frac12\ge\delta_0,
\qquad
P\{z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\}=1\ge c_X,
\tag{12}
\]
so \(\texttt{ass:interior-event-path}\) and \(\texttt{ass:positive-query-region}\) hold.

Define
\[
\Gamma_\eta=\mathbf1\{X_1\le\eta\}.
\tag{13}
\]
The two causal completions have the same historical and donor variables.  Under the zero-effect completion \(P_{0,\eta}\), set
\[
B_{1i}(0)=B_{1i}(1)=B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=8.
\tag{14}
\]
Under the nonzero-effect completion \(P_{1,\eta}\), set
\[
B_{1i}(0)=8,
\qquad
B_{1i}(1)=B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=8+\Gamma_\eta.
\tag{15}
\]
For both completions, define \(B_{1i}(a,\mathbf a_{-1i})=B_{1i}(a)\) for all other-unit assignments and \(Q_{1ti}(a)=Q_{1ti}\) for \(a\in\{0,1\}\).  Equations (14)--(15) and these extensions verify, respectively, \(\texttt{ass:consistency}\), \(\texttt{ass:historical-consistency}\), \(\texttt{ass:no-spillovers}\), and \(\texttt{ass:limited-anticipation}\).  They also give
\[
0\le B_{1i}(a)\le9<B,
\tag{16}
\]
which is \(\texttt{ass:bounded-event-wealth}\).  To realize \(\texttt{def:buyhold-level}\), take
\[
W_{1i,-1}=1,
\qquad
R_{1i0}(a)=B_{1i}(a)-1>-1.
\tag{17}
\]
Then \(W_{1i,-1}\{1+R_{1i0}(a)\}=B_{1i}(a)\), as required because \(H=0\).

The untreated event potential outcome is eight under both completions.  Since \(m(z_0)=8\),
\[
\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,\eta}}[B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0,E_0]
=8=m(z_0),
\qquad \ell\in\{0,1\},
\tag{18}
\]
so \(\texttt{ass:event-transport}\) holds.  Conditional on the complete design and \(E_0\), the event outcomes in (14) or (15) are degenerate, whereas unit \(i\)'s historical path is a function only of the independent vector \((U_{ti})_{t=1}^{T}\).  Hence the complete outcome vectors are independent across \(i\) under this conditioning, which verifies \(\texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence}\).  Equations (5)--(18) therefore verify every member property of \(\texttt{def:panel-law-class}\), and
\[
P_{0,\eta},P_{1,\eta}
\in\mathcal M_{T^2,T,(T^2)}(1).
\tag{19}
\]

This construction also isolates which additional centering condition fails.  From \(\varepsilon_{1ti}=U_{ti}/2\) and independence of the Rademacher errors from the design,
\[
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,\eta}}\!\left[
\varepsilon_{1ti}\,\middle|\,(X_t)_{t=1}^{T},E_0
\right]=0,
\qquad \ell\in\{0,1\},
\tag{20}
\]
so both laws satisfy \(\texttt{ass:historical-full-design-centering}\).  In contrast, under \(P_{1,\eta}\),
\[
\mathbb E[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid(X_t)_{t=1}^{T},E_0]
=8+\Gamma_\eta,
\qquad
\mathbb E[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]=8+\eta.
\tag{21}
\]
Because \(0<\eta<1\), \(\Gamma_\eta\ne\eta\) almost surely, and (21) violates \(\texttt{ass:event-full-design-mean-stability}\).  The zero-effect completion satisfies that condition because both conditional means equal eight.

We next separate the causal targets from the observed event means.  Since \(z_0\) and \(E_0\) are constant, \(\pi_1=1\), and \(P(X_1\le\eta)=\eta\), \(\texttt{def:target}\) and (14)--(15) give
\[
\tau_{0,\eta}:=\tau_n^{P_{0,\eta}}(z_0)=0,
\qquad
\tau_{1,\eta}:=\tau_n^{P_{1,\eta}}(z_0)
=\mathbb E[\Gamma_\eta]=\eta.
\tag{22}
\]
The realized event mean under \(P_{1,\eta}\) is instead \(8+\Gamma_\eta\), a single design-shared Bernoulli shock which replication over \(i\) does not average.

Let \(\mathcal O\) denote the sigma-field generated by all observed variables and let \(\nu_{\ell,\eta}\) be the conditional law of \(\mathcal O\) given \(E_0\) under \(P_{\ell,\eta}\).  On
\[
A_\eta^c=\{X_1>\eta\},
\tag{23}
\]
the two observed-data maps coincide, while on \(A_\eta\) the event vectors are respectively the all-eight and all-nine vectors and hence have disjoint supports.  The greatest measure dominated by both observed-data laws is therefore their common restriction to (23).  Its mass, namely the conditional observed-data overlap or affinity, is exactly
\[
\|\nu_{0,\eta}\wedge\nu_{1,\eta}\|
=P(A_\eta^c\mid E_0)=1-\eta.
\tag{24}
\]

Let \(\widetilde\tau\) be any observed-data-measurable estimator and let \(\mu_\eta=\nu_{0,\eta}\wedge\nu_{1,\eta}\).  Pointwise, for every real \(x\),
\[
x^2+(x-\eta)^2
=2(x-\eta/2)^2+\frac{\eta^2}{2}
\ge\frac{\eta^2}{2}.
\tag{25}
\]
Since \(\mu_\eta\le\nu_{\ell,\eta}\), (22)--(25) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\mathbb E_{P_{0,\eta}}[(\widetilde\tau-\tau_{0,\eta})^2\mid E_0]
+\mathbb E_{P_{1,\eta}}[(\widetilde\tau-\tau_{1,\eta})^2\mid E_0]\\
&\qquad\ge
\int\{\widetilde\tau^2+(\widetilde\tau-\eta)^2\}\,d\mu_\eta
\ge(1-\eta)\frac{\eta^2}{2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{26}
\]
At least one summand in (26) is at least half its right side.  By (19),
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\tau}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{T^2,T,(T^2)}(1)}
\mathbb E_P[\{\widetilde\tau-\tau_n(z_0)\}^2\mid E_0]
\ge\frac{(1-\eta)\eta^2}{4}.
\tag{27}
\]
Taking \(\eta=1/4\) in (27) yields the asserted constant \(3/256\).

For this array, \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\) gives
\[
R_{\mathrm{tr}}=T^{-2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{sm}}=(T^3)^{-2/3}=T^{-2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{don}}=T^{-2},
\tag{28}
\]
and
\[
R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}
=\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{2}.
\tag{29}
\]
Thus, for all sufficiently large \(T\),
\[
R_{\star,\beta}=R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\longrightarrow0,
\tag{30}
\]
whereas the lower bound (27) is constant.  This proves the universal risk obstruction over the original class.

For the interval obstruction, fix \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\) and define
\[
\eta_\alpha=\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}.
\tag{31}
\]
Then \(\eta_\alpha\in(0,1/2)\) and
\[
1-\eta_\alpha-2\alpha=\eta_\alpha>0,
\qquad
1-\eta_\alpha>2\alpha.
\tag{32}
\]
Let \(I\) be an observed-data-measurable interval which is conditionally honest uniformly over the original class.  Applied to the pair with \(\eta=\eta_\alpha\), honesty and (22) give
\[
P_{0,\eta_\alpha}\{0\notin I\mid E_0\}\le\alpha,
\qquad
P_{1,\eta_\alpha}\{\eta_\alpha\notin I\mid E_0\}\le\alpha.
\tag{33}
\]
With \(\mu_{\eta_\alpha}\) as above, measure subadditivity, domination by the two laws, (24), and (33) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mu_{\eta_\alpha}\{0,\eta_\alpha\in I\}
&\ge \mu_{\eta_\alpha}(\Omega)
-\mu_{\eta_\alpha}\{0\notin I\}
-\mu_{\eta_\alpha}\{\eta_\alpha\notin I\}\\
&\ge1-\eta_\alpha-2\alpha
=\eta_\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\tag{34}
\]
Whenever an interval contains both zero and \(\eta_\alpha\), its length is at least \(\eta_\alpha\).  Since \(\mu_{\eta_\alpha}\le\nu_{0,\eta_\alpha}\), (34) implies
\[
\mathbb E_{P_{0,\eta_\alpha}}[\operatorname{length}(I)\mid E_0]
\ge\int\operatorname{length}(I)\,d\mu_{\eta_\alpha}
\ge\eta_\alpha^2.
\tag{35}
\]
Taking the supremum over the original class and then the infimum over all uniformly honest intervals proves the asserted honest-length lower bound.  Equations (20)--(21) show precisely that this impossibility proves rate-essentiality of the event-side restriction but not separate necessity of the historical restriction.

It remains to retain the estimator-specific corollaries for \(\eta=1/4\).  Work henceforth under \(P_{1,1/4}\), abbreviate \(\Gamma=\Gamma_{1/4}\), and note from (15) and (22) that
\[
\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}=8+\Gamma,
\qquad
\tau_n(z_0)=\frac14.
\tag{36}
\]
The generated and projected centers satisfy
\[
\bar Z=\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^{N}Z_j,
\qquad
\widetilde z=\Pi_{[0,1]}(\bar Z).
\tag{37}
\]
Projection fixes \(z_0\) and is nonexpansive.  Using (8)--(9) and \(N=T^2\),
\[
|\widetilde z-z_0|
\le\left|\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^{N}V_j\right|,
\qquad
\mathbb E[(\widetilde z-z_0)^2\mid E_0]
\le N^{-1}=T^{-2}.
\tag{38}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(T\), the truncation at one in the beta-mixing initial bandwidth is inactive, and (28)--(29) imply
\[
\underline h_T
=C_h\left[T^{-1}\vee\frac{\log T}{T}\vee T^{-1}\right]
=C_h\frac{\log T}{T}.
\tag{39}
\]
Define
\[
I_T=\{t:|X_t-\widetilde z|\le\underline h_T\},
\qquad
\mathcal A_T=\{|I_T|>0\}.
\tag{40}
\]
For every \(\widetilde z\in[0,1]\), the intersection of \([\widetilde z-\underline h_T,\widetilde z+\underline h_T]\) with \([0,1]\) has Lebesgue measure at least \(\underline h_T\).  Donor independence and the iid uniform design therefore give
\[
P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0,\widetilde z)
\le(1-\underline h_T)^T
\le e^{-T\underline h_T}
=T^{-C_h},
\tag{41}
\]
so \(P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0)\to0\).

On \(\mathcal A_T\), the first candidate has
\[
L_1=n_1|I_T|,
\qquad
G_1=n_1|I_T|,
\qquad
\lambda_{\min}(G_1/L_1)=1\ge c_G.
\tag{42}
\]
Thus the selector accepts it, and the local-constant fit is
\[
\widehat m_1
=\frac1{n_1|I_T|}
\sum_{t\in I_T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}Q_{1ti}.
\tag{43}
\]
The conditional-mean part of (43) differs from \(m(z_0)=8\) by at most
\[
\frac1{|I_T|}\sum_{t\in I_T}|m(X_t)-m(z_0)|
\le\underline h_T+|\widetilde z-z_0|.
\tag{44}
\]
Given the design and donors, the noise part has mean zero and variance
\[
\operatorname{Var}\!\left(
\frac1{2n_1|I_T|}\sum_{t\in I_T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}U_{ti}
\,\middle|\,(X_t)_{t=1}^{T},(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N},E_0
\right)
=\frac1{4n_1|I_T|}
\le\frac1{4n_1}.
\tag{45}
\]
Every successful local-constant intercept is an average of values in \([7,9]\), while the failed-fit rule sets it to zero.  Hence \((\widehat m_1-8)^2\le64\) on \(\mathcal A_T^c\).  Splitting over \(\mathcal A_T\), using \((x+y)^2\le2x^2+2y^2\), and applying (38), (39), (41), (44), and (45), there is a fixed \(C<\infty\) such that
\[
\mathbb E[(\widehat m_1-8)^2\mid E_0]
\le C\{\underline h_T^2+N^{-1}+n_1^{-1}
+P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0)\}
\longrightarrow0.
\tag{46}
\]
Put \(D_T=\widehat m_1-8\).  By (36) and \(\texttt{def:feasible-estimator}\),
\[
\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)=\Gamma-\frac14-D_T.
\tag{47}
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz and (46) yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\left|
\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
-\mathbb E[(\Gamma-1/4)^2\mid E_0]
\right|\\
&\quad\le
2\{\mathbb E[(\Gamma-1/4)^2\mid E_0]\}^{1/2}
\{\mathbb E[D_T^2\mid E_0]\}^{1/2}
+\mathbb E[D_T^2\mid E_0]
\longrightarrow0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{48}
\]
Since \(\Gamma\) is Bernoulli with success probability \(1/4\),
\[
\lim_{T\to\infty}
\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
=\operatorname{Var}(\Gamma)
=\frac14\left(1-\frac14\right)
=\frac3{16}.
\tag{49}
\]
The no-log spacing term is \(R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-2}\); together with (28), this gives \(R_\star=T^{-2}\).

Finally consider \(C_\alpha\).  On \(\mathcal A_T\), (42)--(43) give
\[
a_{1ti}=\frac{\mathbf1\{t\in I_T\}}{n_1|I_T|},
\qquad
\sum_t|a_{1ti}|=\frac1{n_1},
\qquad
\sum_{t,i}|a_{1ti}|=1.
\tag{50}
\]
For fixed \(\alpha\), substitution into \(\texttt{def:honest-interval}\) yields
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}
=B\left\{\frac12\log\left(\frac2{\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}}\right)n_1^{-1}\right\}^{1/2}
=O(T^{-1}),
\tag{51}
\]
\[
R_{\mathrm{evt}}
=B\left\{\frac12\log\left(\frac2{\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}}\right)n_1^{-1}\right\}^{1/2}
=O(T^{-1}).
\tag{52}
\]
The support of \(K\), (39), and (50) give
\[
A_L\le C_{0,1}L\underline h_T
=O\!\left(\frac{\log T}{T}\right).
\tag{53}
\]
Here \(D=1\), so the exact donor calibration satisfies
\[
M_4(N)=\frac{16}{N}+3\left(1-\frac1N\right)\le16,
\qquad
q_N=\{M_4(N)/\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}\}^{1/4}=O(1).
\tag{54}
\]
By (2), \(N=T^2\), and \(\kappa=1\),
\[
\delta_N=\frac{q_N}{\sqrt N}=O(T^{-1}),
\qquad
A_{\mathrm{don}}=\delta_N=O(T^{-1}).
\tag{55}
\]
Thus \(\delta_N\le\delta_0\) eventually.  On \(\mathcal A_T\), the selected Gram matrix is positive and all required quantities are finite.  Consequently the fallback event is contained in \(\mathcal A_T^c\) for all sufficiently large \(T\), and, throughout \(\mathcal A_T\),
\[
H_\alpha
=R_{\mathrm{hist}}+R_{\mathrm{evt}}+A_L+A_{\mathrm{don}}
=O\!\left(\frac{\log T}{T}\right)
=o(1).
\tag{56}
\]
In particular, \(H_\alpha<1/8\) eventually on \(\mathcal A_T\).

If the nonfallback interval contains \(\tau_n(z_0)\), then \(|\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)|\le H_\alpha\).  Yet \(|\Gamma-1/4|\ge1/4\) surely, so (47) and the reverse triangle inequality imply on \(\{|D_T|<1/16\}\) that
\[
|\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)|
\ge\frac14-\frac1{16}
=\frac3{16}>\frac18.
\tag{57}
\]
Equations (56)--(57) show that, eventually,
\[
\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\}
\subseteq \mathcal A_T^c\cup\{|D_T|\ge1/16\}.
\tag{58}
\]
Markov's inequality and (46) now give
\[
\begin{aligned}
P\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid E_0\}
&\le P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0)
+P(|D_T|\ge1/16\mid E_0)\\
&\le P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0)
+256\,\mathbb E[D_T^2\mid E_0]
\longrightarrow0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{59}
\]
This proves both estimator-specific corollaries and completes the proof.

\[
R_\star=T^{-2},
\qquad
\lim_{T\to\infty}\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\{\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)\}^2\,\middle|\,E_0
\right]=\frac{3}{16},
\]
and, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\),
\[

\]

\lim_{T\to\infty}\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\{\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)\}^2\,\middle|\,E_0
\right]=\frac{3}{16},
\]
and, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\),
\[
P\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid E_0\}\longrightarrow0.
\]

project_justification.niche: The panel architecture observes historical proxy paths exactly, replicates untreated wealth blocks at each calendar window, and estimates only the event-date query from an independent donor sample.  It separates unit replication, calendar path coverage, generated-center uncertainty, and shared-design event shocks.  The resulting maximality witness shows why event full-design mean stability is rate-essential, while the restricted positive theory exposes a dependence elbow: design-only geometric beta mixing costs a logarithm in uniform spacing, whereas conditional calendar independence removes it.
project_justification.fill: The project proves event-transport identification, a universal impossibility over the original class, exact weighted-panel algebra on the full-design-centered class, feasible full-donor local-polynomial estimators, and exact finite-sample conditionally honest intervals.  The impossibility uses two admissible causal completions with fixed observed-data overlap and target separation; it proves constant minimax-risk and honest-length lower bounds even when the candidate frontier vanishes.  The maintained beta-mixing restricted class has frontier \(R_{\star,\beta}\); the named independent-calendar full-design-centered subclass has the sharp no-log frontier \(R_\star\) for every \(\lambda>0\).  For fixed \(B>D^2\), all four lower channels match in both restricted regimes.  At \(B=D^2\), the upper bounds persist and the universal converse contains treated, smoothing, and the dependence-appropriate spacing channel only.  No donor splitting, covariance estimator, deconvolution, dense-site assumption, upper local-mass condition, or sequential overlap is used.

proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(D=Sd\).  By \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding}, the standardized fourth-moment and covariance requirements force \(B\ge D^2\), so the class is empty when \(B<D^2\).  We therefore prove the two nonempty cases separately.

First suppose \(B>D^2\).  For each \(q\in\{\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{sm},\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{don}\}\), let \((P_{0,q},P_{1,q})\) be the conditional two-point experiment supplied by \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding}.  Write
\[
\theta_{\ell,q}=\tau_{n,P_{\ell,q}}(z_0),
\qquad
\Delta_q=|\theta_{1,q}-\theta_{0,q}|.
\]
That lemma gives constants \(a_{q,>}>0\) and \(c_{q,>}>0\), independent of \(N,T,\mathbf n\), such that, for almost every admissible \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\), the conditional overlap of the two observed-data laws is at least \(a_{q,>}\) and
\[
\Delta_q^2\ge c_{q,>}R_q.
\tag{1}
\]
For an arbitrary observed-data estimator \(\widetilde\tau\), define
\[
A_{0,q}=\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_{0,q}|\ge\Delta_q/2\},
\qquad
A_{1,q}=\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_{1,q}|\ge\Delta_q/2\}.
\]
The triangle inequality implies \(A_{0,q}\cup A_{1,q}\) is the entire sample space.  Integrating its indicator against the overlap measure therefore yields
\[
P_{0,q}(A_{0,q}\mid E_0)+P_{1,q}(A_{1,q}\mid E_0)
\ge a_{q,>}.
\tag{2}
\]
It follows from (1)--(2) that
\[
\begin{aligned}
\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}
 [ (\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\ell,q})^2\mid E_0]
&\ge {\Delta_q^2\over4}
 \max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}P_{\ell,q}(A_{\ell,q}\mid E_0)\\
&\ge {a_{q,>}\Delta_q^2\over8}
\ge {a_{q,>}c_{q,>}\over8}R_q.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
There are only four channels.  Taking their maximum in (3), and using the definition
\(R_{\star,\beta}=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}\), proves the strict-slack minimax lower bound with a constant \(c_{>}>0\).  The donor-channel constants, and hence \(c_{>}\), may depend on the fixed slack \(B-D^2\).

If \(B=D^2\), the boundary clause of \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding} supplies the same argument with independently quantified overlap and separation constants for precisely \(q\in\{\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{sm},\mathrm{sp}\}\).  Maximizing (3) over those three channels gives
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\ge c_{=}
\{R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\}
\tag{4}
\]
for a separately chosen \(c_{=}>0\).  No donor lower experiment is used at equality.

It remains to prove the common upper bound.  Let
\[
\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:1\le s\le S,\ 1\le t\le T\},
\qquad
\mathscr G=\sigma\{\mathscr X,E_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_N\}.
\]
Because \(z_0=\mathbb E_P[Z_j\mid E_0]\) is \(E_0\)-measurable, conditioning additionally on \(z_0\) does not alter an \(E_0\)-conditional mean.  On the good sample, \texttt{lem:identification-fwl}, the linear representation in \texttt{def:honest-interval}, and \(Q_{sti}=m_s(X_{st})+\varepsilon_{sti}\) give the exact identity
\[
\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)
=U_{\mathrm{evt}}-U_{\mathrm{hist}}-B_{\mathrm{LP}}-B_{\mathrm{don}},
\tag{5}
\]
where
\[
U_{\mathrm{evt}}
=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}{\pi_s\over n_s}
\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\},
\tag{6}
\]
\[
U_{\mathrm{hist}}
=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\pi_s
\sum_{t=1}^{T}a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti},
\tag{7}
\]
\[
B_{\mathrm{LP}}
=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
\left\{\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}a_{sti}m_s(X_{st})
-m_s(\widetilde z_s)\right\},
\tag{8}
\]
and
\[
B_{\mathrm{don}}
=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{m_s(\widetilde z_s)-m_s(z_{0s})\}.
\tag{9}
\]
The event full-design mean-stability assumption centers every summand in (6) conditionally on \(\mathscr X\) and \(E_0\); the historical full-design centering assumption does the same for every error in (7).  Donor independence permits adjoining \((Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}\) to that conditioning.  Conditional cross-unit independence then makes the unit-level terms in each of (6) and (7) independent across distinct \((s,i)\).  Since every event wealth lies in \([0,B]\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[U_{\mathrm{evt}}^2\mid\mathscr G]
\le B^2\sum_{s=1}^{S}{\pi_s^2\over n_s}
=B^2R_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\tag{10}
\]
Likewise, conditional on \(\mathscr G\), the range of the unit-level random variable \(\sum_t a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}\) has length at most \(B\sum_t|a_{sti}|\), because \(0\le Q_{sti}\le B\) and the regression means are then fixed.  Hence \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control} gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P[U_{\mathrm{hist}}^2\mid\mathscr G]
&\le B^2\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
 \left[\pi_s\sum_{t=1}^{T}|a_{sti}|\right]^2\\
&\le B^2c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
Thus neither calculation requires identical unit response laws or temporal independence of the outcomes.

We next control (8).  On a successful fit, the definition of \(a_{sti}\) and invertibility of \(G_s\) imply polynomial reproduction:
\[
\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}a_{sti}b_r(u_{st})
=G_sG_s^{-1}e_0=e_0.
\tag{12}
\]
Let \(C_K<\infty\) be a fixed Euclidean radius of the compact support of \(K\).  A nonzero weight entails
\(\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_s\|_2\le C_Kh_s\).  Applying the degree-\(r\) Taylor remainder in the declared H\"older ball, using (12) to reproduce the Taylor polynomial at \(\widetilde z_s\), and then invoking the absolute-weight bound in \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control}, we obtain
\[
\left|\sum_{t,i}a_{sti}m_s(X_{st})-m_s(\widetilde z_s)\right|
\le C L h_s^\lambda\sum_{t,i}|a_{sti}|
\le C h_s^\lambda.
\tag{13}
\]
Since \(S\) is fixed, Cauchy--Schwarz and \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control} with exponent \(2\lambda\), first conditionally on \((E_0,\widetilde z_s)\) and then integrated over the donor sample, show that
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P[B_{\mathrm{LP}}^2\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0]
&\le C\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s^2
 \mathbb E_P[h_s^{2\lambda}\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0]\\
&\le C\left\{
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s^2(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
+\left({\log(T\vee2)\over T}\right)^{2\lambda/d}
+N^{-\lambda}\right\}\\
&\le C R_{\star,\beta},
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
\]
where the last inequality uses \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\), and hence \(N^{-\lambda}\le N^{-\kappa}\).

For (9), define the proof-only standardized variables
\[
Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0),
\qquad
W_N=N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{N}Y_j.
\]
Conditional donor replication, the definition of \(z_0\), and the definition of \(\Sigma\) imply
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y_j\mid E_0]=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[Y_jY_j^\top\mid E_0]=I_D,
\]
with the \(Y_j\)'s conditionally independent.  Expanding the fourth power of the Euclidean norm, all products containing a singleton sample index vanish.  The all-equal terms and the three pairings therefore give exactly
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P[\|W_N\|_2^4\mid E_0]
&={1\over N}\mathbb E_P[\|Y_1\|_2^4\mid E_0]\\
&\quad+\left(1-{1\over N}\right)
\{(\operatorname{tr}I_D)^2+2\operatorname{tr}(I_D^2)\}\\
&\le {B\over N}+\left(1-{1\over N}\right)(D^2+2D)
=M_4(N).
\end{aligned}
\tag{15}
\]
Consequently,
\[
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\bar Z-z_0)\|_2^4\mid E_0
\right]
\le C N^{-2}.
\tag{16}
\]
Euclidean projection on the closed cube cannot increase distance from the cube point \(z_0\).  Combining this fact with
\(c_\Sigma I_D\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_D\) yields
\[
V_N:=\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\widetilde z-z_0)\|_2
\le \sqrt{C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma}\,
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\bar Z-z_0)\|_2.
\tag{17}
\]
On \(\{V_N\le\delta_0\}\), the displacement \(\widetilde z-z_0\) is feasible in \texttt{def:local-modulus}; its upper modulus bound gives
\[
|B_{\mathrm{don}}|\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}V_N^\kappa.
\tag{18}
\]
By Lyapunov's inequality, (16)--(18), and \(0<\kappa\le1\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{\mathrm{don}}^2
 \mathbf1\{V_N\le\delta_0\}\mid E_0]
\le C\{\mathbb E_P[V_N^4\mid E_0]\}^{\kappa/2}
\le C N^{-\kappa}.
\tag{19}
\]
Because \(m_s\) takes values in \([0,B]\) and the positive cohort weights sum to one, \(|B_{\mathrm{don}}|\le B\) everywhere.  Markov's inequality and (16)--(17) thus imply
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{\mathrm{don}}^2
 \mathbf1\{V_N>\delta_0\}\mid E_0]
\le B^2P(V_N>\delta_0\mid E_0)
\le C N^{-2}
\le C N^{-\kappa}.
\tag{20}
\]
Equations (19)--(20) prove
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{\mathrm{don}}^2\mid E_0]
\le C R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{21}
\]
Only the covariance eigenvalue bounds and standardized fourth-moment envelope were used; in particular, neither Gaussianity, coordinate homoskedasticity, nor estimation of \(\Sigma\) is required.

It remains to account for the fallback event.  On a successful fit,
\[
|\widehat m_s|
\le B\sum_{t,i}|a_{sti}|
\le Bc_G^{-1/2}
\tag{22}
\]
by \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control}, whereas the failed-fit rule sets the intercept contribution to zero.  Event averages and the causal target are bounded by the declared wealth envelope.  Hence \((\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\) is bounded by a fixed constant on the bad sample.  The total bad-sample probability bound in \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control} makes its conditional risk contribution at most \(CR_{\star,\beta}\) along every array in the theorem.

Finally, apply \((x_1+x_2+x_3+x_4)^2\le4\sum_{j=1}^{4}x_j^2\) to (5), integrate (10)--(11), and combine the result with (14), (21), and the bad-sample bound.  Uniformly over the full-design-centered class,
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\le C R_{\star,\beta}.
\tag{23}
\]
The constants in (23) depend only on fixed class and procedural constants.  They may be named \(C_{>}\) in the strict-slack regime and, independently, \(C_{=}\) in the equality-boundary regime.  Because \(\widehat\tau\) is an observed-data estimator, the minimax infimum is no larger than its worst-case risk.  Combining (23) with (3) for \(B>D^2\), or with (4) for \(B=D^2\), proves all displayed bounds.  The selector result used in (14) assumes only the declared geometric beta-mixing envelope, so the construction requires no sequential-overlap or anti-clustering condition.

Put \(D=Sd\).  The compatibility calculation in
\texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding} gives
\[
D^2\le
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\left\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_1-z_0)\right\|_2^4
\,\middle|\,E_0\right]
\le B.
\tag{66}
\]
Thus the class is empty when \(B<D^2\), and there is no substantive
minimax assertion in that case.  Fix henceforth \(B\ge D^2\),
\(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), and an admissible
event state outside a conditional null set.  Let
\[
\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:1\le s\le S,\ 1\le t\le T\}.
\]
Because \(z_0\) is measurable with respect to \(E_0\), conditioning on
\((z_0,E_0)\) is the same as conditioning on \(E_0\) for the quantities
below.

We first prove finite-sample conditional coverage.  On each successful fit,
polynomial reproduction from \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control},
applied to the degree-\(r\) Taylor polynomial of \(m_s\) at
\(\widetilde z_s\), gives
\[
\left|
e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_s-m_s(\widetilde z_s)
-\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}
\right|
\le
C_{r,d}L\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}|a_{sti}|
\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_s\|_2^\lambda.
\tag{67}
\]
After multiplication by the cohort weights and summation over \(s\), the
right-hand side is exactly \(A_L\).

Define the historical unit-cluster variables
\[
\mathsf H_{si}=\pi_s\sum_{t=1}^{T}a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:historical-full-design-centering} centers these
variables given \((\mathscr X,E_0)\).  Assumption
\texttt{ass:donor-independence} preserves the centering after adjoining all
donors, and \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} gives independence over
\((s,i)\) under this conditioning.  By
\texttt{ass:bounded-historical-wealth}, conditional on the complete design
the range length of \(\mathsf H_{si}\) is at most
\[
c_{si}=B\pi_s\sum_{t=1}^{T}|a_{sti}|.
\]
For completeness, if a conditionally centered random variable \(U\) lies in
an interval of length \(c\), convexity of \(x\mapsto e^{vx}\) bounds its
conditional exponential moment by the endpoint mixture with the same mean;
differentiating the logarithm of that two-point mixture yields
\[
\mathbb E[e^{vU}\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}]
\le e^{v^2c^2/8}.
\tag{68}
\]
Multiplying (68) over the conditionally independent unit clusters, applying
the exponential Markov inequality, optimizing over \(v>0\), and repeating
the argument for \(-U\) give
\[
P_P\!\left\{
\left|\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathsf H_{si}\right|
>R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}
\right\}
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}.
\tag{69}
\]
Thus a unit's whole calendar history is one bounded cluster; no temporal
outcome mixing is used.

Similarly, define
\[
\mathsf E_{si}=\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\left\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}
-\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\right\}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:event-full-design-mean-stability} centers
\(\mathsf E_{si}\) given \((\mathscr X,E_0)\); donor independence preserves
this centering after donors are adjoined, and cross-unit independence again
gives conditional independence.  By \texttt{ass:bounded-event-wealth}, their
conditional range lengths are at most \(B\pi_s/n_s\).  The same exponential
moment calculation therefore gives
\[
P_P\!\left\{
\left|\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathsf E_{si}\right|
>R_{\mathrm{evt}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}
\right\}
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}.
\tag{70}
\]
A union bound combines (69) and (70); independence between one unit's
historical path and event outcome is not required.

For donor calibration, define only in this proof
\[
Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0),
\qquad
W_N=N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{N}Y_j.
\]
By the definition of \(z_0\), \(\mathbb E_P[Y_j\mid E_0]=0\), and by the
definition of \(\Sigma\) and \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity},
\(\mathbb E_P[Y_jY_j^\top\mid E_0]=I_D\).  Conditional independent donor
replication and expansion of \(\|\sum_jY_j\|_2^4\) show that the terms whose
indices occur once vanish, while the pairings contribute
\(D^2+2D\).  Using \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment},
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P[\|W_N\|_2^4\mid E_0]
&=\frac1N\mathbb E_P[\|Y_1\|_2^4\mid E_0]
+\left(1-\frac1N\right)(D^2+2D)\\
&\le \frac BN+\left(1-\frac1N\right)(D^2+2D)
=M_4(N).
\end{aligned}
\tag{71}
\]
Let \(\mathcal D_N=\{\|W_N\|_2\le q_N\}\).  Markov's inequality and the
definition of \(q_N\) imply
\[
P_P(\mathcal D_N^c\mid E_0)
\le \frac{M_4(N)}{q_N^4}=\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{72}
\]
Projection onto the closed convex cube \(([0,1]^d)^S\) cannot increase
Euclidean distance from \(z_0\), since \(z_0\) belongs to that cube.  The
covariance eigenvalue bounds therefore give, on \(\mathcal D_N\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\widetilde z-z_0)\|_2
&\le c_\Sigma^{-1/2}\|\widetilde z-z_0\|_2\\
&\le c_\Sigma^{-1/2}\|\bar Z-z_0\|_2\\
&\le \sqrt{C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma}\,q_N/\sqrt N
=\delta_N.
\end{aligned}
\tag{73}
\]
On the good sample in \texttt{def:honest-interval},
\(\delta_N\le\delta_0\).  Hence the upper half of
\texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus} and (73) imply
\[
\left|
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
\{m_s(\widetilde z_s)-m_s(z_{0s})\}
\right|
\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta_N^\kappa=A_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{74}
\]

Let \(\mathcal G\) be the selector-and-radius good event from
\texttt{def:honest-interval}; it is measurable with respect to
\((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N})\).  On \(\mathcal G^c\), the interval is
the fallback \([-B,B]\).  Assumptions \texttt{ass:bounded-event-wealth} and
the positive weights summing to one imply \(\tau_n(z_0)\in[-B,B]\).  On
\(\mathcal G\cap\mathcal D_N\), \texttt{lem:identification-fwl}, (67), and
(74) decompose \(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)\) into the event fluctuation, the
negative of the historical fluctuation, and two remainders bounded in
absolute value by \(A_L\) and \(A_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Thus noncoverage there
implies failure of (69) or (70).  Iterated conditioning and Bonferroni's
inequality give, for every positive \(N,T,n_1,\ldots,n_S\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_P\{\tau_n(z_0)\notin C_\alpha\mid E_0\}
&\le P_P(\mathcal D_N^c\mid E_0)\\
&\quad+
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\mathbf 1_{\mathcal G\cap\mathcal D_N}
P_P\!\left\{
\text{historical failure or event failure}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}
\right\}
\,\middle|\,E_0\right]\\
&\le \alpha_{\mathrm{don}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}
+\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}=\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\tag{75}
\]
No selector-tail probability enters (75), so coverage is exact and
finite-sample, including at \(B=D^2\).  Intersecting the untruncated interval
with \([-B,B]\) cannot remove the target.

We next prove the expected-length upper bound.  The deterministic bounds in
\texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control} yield on every successful
fit
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\le B\left\{
\frac12\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}})c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}
\right\}^{1/2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{evt}}
=B\left\{
\frac12\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}})R_{\mathrm{tr}}
\right\}^{1/2}.
\tag{76}
\]
Compact support of \(K\) and the same deterministic bound on
\(\sum_{t,i}|a_{sti}|\) give
\[
A_L\le C\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_sh_s^\lambda
\quad\text{on }\mathcal G.
\tag{77}
\]
Apply \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control} with exponent
\(a=\lambda\), conditionally on the projected donor center.  Since \(S\) is
fixed, Cauchy--Schwarz across cohorts, \(\sum_s\pi_s=1\), and
\(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sup_P\mathbb E_P[A_L\mathbf 1_{\mathcal G}\mid E_0]
&\le C\left\{
R_{\mathrm{sm}}^{1/2}
+R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}^{1/2}+N^{-\lambda/2}
\right\}\\
&\le CR_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{78}
\]
Because \(D,B,\alpha\) are fixed, (71) implies \(q_N\le C\), whence
\[
A_{\mathrm{don}}
\le CN^{-\kappa/2}=CR_{\mathrm{don}}^{1/2}.
\tag{79}
\]
The selector lemma also gives
\(P_P(\mathcal G^c\mid E_0)\le CR_{\star,\beta}\) along every asserted
array.  On \(\mathcal G\), interval length is at most \(2H_\alpha\); on
\(\mathcal G^c\), it is at most \(2B\).  Since
\(R_{\star,\beta}\to0\) along those arrays, eventually
\(R_{\star,\beta}\le R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\).  Combining (76)--(79) proves,
with a constant independently quantified in each compatible envelope
regime,
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid E_0]
\le C_\alpha^{\mathrm{up}}R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\tag{80}
\]

It remains to establish the expected-length converse.  The treated,
smoothing, and donor constructions in \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding} have
perturbation constants that may be decreased while remaining fixed along the
array.  Their displayed divergence calculations then make the testing
affinity arbitrarily close to one while retaining separation by a positive
fixed multiple of \(R_q^{1/2}\).  In the spacing construction in
\texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-spacing-obstruction}, decreasing its fixed
rare-block probability constant makes the no-active-block probability, and
hence the testing affinity, arbitrarily close to one while retaining a
positive fixed multiple of \(R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}^{1/2}\).  Therefore, for
the fixed \(\alpha<1/2\), the construction constants may be selected so that
every available channel affinity
\[
A_q=\int\min\{dP_{0,q},dP_{1,q}\}
\]
exceeds \(2\alpha+a_0\) for some fixed \(a_0>0\).  In the donor channel the
choice, and hence the resulting lower-bound constant, may depend on the
fixed slack \(B-D^2\).

Let \(I\) be any finite-sample conditionally honest observed-data interval,
write the two targets in a channel pair as \(\theta_0,\theta_1\), and let
\(\mu_q=P_{0,q}\wedge P_{1,q}\) denote the conditional overlap measure.
Uniform conditional honesty implies
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mu_q\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I\}
&\ge \mu_q(\Omega)
-P_{0,q}\{\theta_0\notin I\mid E_0\}
-P_{1,q}\{\theta_1\notin I\mid E_0\}\\
&\ge A_q-2\alpha\ge a_0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{81}
\]
On this event, \(\operatorname{length}(I)\ge|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).
Consequently,
\[
\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}[\operatorname{length}(I)\mid E_0]
\ge \int\operatorname{length}(I)\,d\mu_q
\ge a_0|\theta_1-\theta_0|
\ge c_\alpha R_q^{1/2}.
\tag{82}
\]
For a fixed interior-compatible envelope \(B>D^2\), all four pairs in
\texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding} are available.  Maximizing (82) over
\(q\in\{\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{sm},\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{don}\}\) gives
\(c_{\alpha,>}R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\), with dependence on the fixed slack
allowed.  At \(B=D^2\), only the treated, smoothing, and spacing pairs are
available, so (82) gives
\[
c_{\alpha,=}
\{R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee
R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\}^{1/2};
\tag{83}
\]
no donor converse is used or asserted at equality.  The constants in these
two cases are independently quantified.

Finally, if an interval sequence is only uniformly asymptotically
conditionally honest, then for every \(\epsilon>0\) both noncoverage
probabilities in (81) are eventually at most \(\alpha+\epsilon\).  Taking
\(\epsilon<a_0/4\) leaves overlap probability at least \(a_0/2\), so (82)
and the same rates continue to hold.  Equations (75), (80), and (82)--(83)
prove all asserted coverage and expected-length conclusions.
